Suggest which of a key's species a photo shows

Source: R/names.R
suggestSpecies.Rd

Compares each photo with the names of the key's results and ranks the results by how well they match, so a photo can be checked against the species the key covers. This works best with a model trained on names of organisms, such as BioCLIP 2 (visionModel(name = "bioclip-2")): it recognises a species from its scientific name without being shown any examples. Only the key's own species are considered, which makes the answers much more reliable than asking the model to name a species out of all those it knows.

Usage

suggestSpecies(key, model, paths, top = 3, prompt = "a photo of %s.")

Arguments

key

A dimoose key.

model

A visionModel().

paths

Image files, or an imageSet() (its path column is embedded and its id column names the rows).

top

How many of the best-matching results to return per photo.

prompt

The text each name is put into, with %s where the name goes. The default is the one BioCLIP was trained with.

Value

A data frame with top rows per image: image (its id), rank, Taxon, probability and similarity (cosine similarity).

Details

Each result is described by its scientific name when it is written as "Common name (Genus species)", and by the whole result otherwise. The probabilities are a softmax over all the key's results with the temperature CLIP models are trained with (cosine similarity times 100).

See also

identifyPhotos() for one answer per photo, at the genus or family when the species is uncertain.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
model <- visionModel(name = "bioclip-2")
suggestSpecies(montanaKey(), model, "my-photo.jpg")
} # }
